chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: John Coltrane in Philadelphia and at the Marie Antoinette
summary: McGhee brought Trane to New York in Jimmy Heath's band; Trane practiced all day.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Well, how do you feel about Coltrane's influence on the music?

Well, I was the first one to bring Coltrane to New York. You know, he was in Philly. Jimmy Heath had a big band over there, you know. So I went over and hired the band and brought to New York to play here at the theatre. And Trane was playing alto, so was Little Bird at the time. Trane at that time didn't impress me as being an amazing musician, but later on he did. I mean, like, when he got with Miles he started coming out of wherever he had been hiding, and really got into something as far as playing his horn was concerned. But Trane was an amazing guy. I mean, as soon as he got with Miles' group, he changed altogether. But he used to play all day long. We lived in the same hotel down here on Broadway, at 67th and Broadway, the Marie Antoinette...

Yeah. He used to play all day long there. I'd hear him, he played at 8 o'clock til 8 o'clock at night, then go on down to Birdland and work like a champ! But I mean, something happened to him. I don't know...

Of course, he was coming out of Bird in many ways, and then when he was with Miles, I guess the second time, after he had been with Monk, they did that album called Kind of Blue, which really introduced the modal kind of playing...
And from there, you know, I guess he made Giant Steps, and after that he seemed to start to go into that other...

Another spirit. Well, I don't quite understand where they really wanted to go. But I mean, I'm for it... If they can get out there and make it sound good, then good, I'm for it. But I don't want anyone to say, 'Well, Maggie's an old diehard,' because I'm not an old diehard and I never want to be one.
